prompt: In the answer for `portal.azure.com`, what does a `CNAME` line say?
hint: It is not an address.

choices.text: This name's address, in IPv4
choices.why: That is an `A` record, the last line.

choices.text: The server that answers for the zone
choices.why: That is an `NS` record.

choices.text: An alias: ask about the other name
choices.why: Right. The resolver followed each one for you.

choices.text: How long the answer may be cached
choices.why: That is the TTL, a column of every record.

prompt: Why does the lesson's `dig` use `+nottlid`?
hint: What changes every second?

choices.text: Because TTLs are secret
choices.why: Nothing about a TTL is secret; dig prints it by default.

choices.text: To make the resolver skip its cache
choices.why: It only changes what is printed, not how the question is asked.

choices.text: Because Azure DNS records have no TTL
choices.why: Every record has one; `public.bicep` sets them.

choices.text: The TTL changes every second
choices.why: Right. The column is there on your machine without the option.

prompt: You run the lesson's `dig portal.azure.com` and get a different chain from the transcript. What does that most likely mean?
hint: Look at the first two links' zones.

choices.text: The services picked another path
choices.why: Right. They pick the next link at the moment you ask.

choices.text: Your resolver is broken
choices.why: A different chain is the expected result, not a fault.

choices.text: The portal moved out of Azure
choices.why: The links still name Azure's services; only the choice differs.

choices.text: The transcript was written by hand
choices.why: It was captured; the chain changes between runs, as its own section warns.

prompt: Match each record type to what it holds.
hint: One of them holds a name, never an address, for mail.

pairs.right: a mail server's name and a preference
the name servers of a zone
free text, such as a proof of ownership

prompt: Why can the top of a zone, `shop.example` itself, not be a CNAME?
hint: What records must the top already have?

choices.text: Azure DNS does not support CNAME records
choices.why: `www` in `public.bicep` is one.

choices.text: A CNAME cannot share its name
choices.why: Right. Which is the problem alias records solve.

choices.text: A CNAME at the top would point at itself
choices.why: It could point anywhere; the rule is about sharing the name.

choices.text: The registrar forbids it, not the DNS
choices.why: It is a rule of the DNS itself.

prompt: The shop has created the zone `shop.example` in Azure DNS but changed nothing at the registrar. Who gets answers from the zone?
hint: What tells the internet where the zone is?

choices.text: Everybody, as soon as the zone exists
choices.why: Without the delegation, no resolver is sent to Azure.

choices.text: Those who ask Azure's servers directly
choices.why: Right. The delegation at the registrar is what sends the internet there.

choices.text: Only the virtual networks linked to it
choices.why: Links belong to private zones.

choices.text: Nobody, until Microsoft approves the domain
choices.why: Microsoft approves nothing; the registrar's NS records decide.

prompt: How many name servers does Azure assign to a public zone?
hint: One per top-level domain in the list.

prompt: Why is the compiled output `nameServers` an expression rather than a list of names?
hint: When are the servers chosen?

choices.text: Because Bicep hides the names until deployment for safety
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; the names do not exist yet.

choices.text: Because the four servers are the same for every zone
choices.why: The numbers differ from zone to zone.

choices.text: Because a private zone has no name servers
choices.why: `public.bicep` is a public zone.

choices.text: Because Azure picks them when the zone is created
choices.why: Right. Nobody knows them before, the compiler included.

prompt: `dig NS shop.example +short` lists two of the four Azure name servers. What is the state of the delegation?
hint: Does it work, and how well?

choices.text: Working, and half as resilient as it should be
choices.why: Right. Write all four at the registrar.

choices.text: Broken: no resolver will reach the zone
choices.why: Two correct servers are enough to answer.

choices.text: Correct: Azure answers with two at a time
choices.why: Azure gave four, and the parent should name all of them.

choices.text: Pending until the other two are approved
choices.why: There is nothing to approve; the registrar lists what it was given.

prompt: The shop deletes `pip-shop-web`. Its zone has an alias `A` at `@` pointing at it, and an old plain `A` at `old` holding the same address typed by hand. Which one becomes a dangling record?
hint: Which record knows the resource is gone?

choices.text: The alias at `@`
choices.why: An alias follows the resource and answers nothing once it is gone.

choices.text: Both, until the TTL runs out
choices.why: The alias stops answering; only the typed one goes on.

choices.text: The plain `A` at `old`
choices.why: Right. It keeps pointing at an address that may now be somebody else's.

choices.text: Neither: Azure deletes records that name a deleted address
choices.why: Azure has no way to know a typed address belonged to that resource.

prompt: What can an Azure DNS alias record set point at? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four kinds of target are named.

choices.text: A public IP address resource
choices.why: Right. `pip-shop-web` in the file.

choices.text: A Traffic Manager profile
choices.why: Right. Lesson 22 builds one.

choices.text: A virtual machine's private address
choices.why: Private addresses belong in private zones.

choices.text: Another record set in the same zone
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A zone in another DNS provider
choices.why: An alias points at Azure resources.

prompt: In a record set's name, `___` stands for the top of the zone.
hint: One character.

prompt: Who can ask the private zone `shop.internal` a question?
hint: What does a virtual network link do?

choices.text: Anybody who knows Azure's name servers
choices.why: Those serve public zones. Private zones have no public servers.

choices.text: Every network in the same subscription
choices.why: A subscription grants nothing; the link does.

choices.text: Machines in the virtual networks linked to it
choices.why: Right. Through `168.63.129.16`.

choices.text: The office, through the VPN, with no further setup
choices.why: The office needs a forwarder to the Private Resolver.

prompt: What does `registrationEnabled: true` on the link do?
hint: Nobody keeps a list.

choices.text: Machines register their own names
choices.why: Right. One registration zone per network.

choices.text: Private endpoints register their addresses in the zone
choices.why: Their records come from zone groups, as in lesson 19.

choices.text: The zone is registered with a public registrar
choices.why: A private zone has nothing to do with registrars.

choices.text: The network may resolve names in the zone
choices.why: Any link lets it resolve; registration is the extra.

prompt: The shop creates a private zone `shop.example` holding only `api`, linked to `vnet-shop-prod`. What happens to `www.shop.example` for machines in that network?
hint: Does a private zone fall through?

choices.text: It resolves from the public zone as before
choices.why: A private zone does not fall through to the public one.

choices.text: It resolves to `api`'s address
choices.why: Nothing maps `www` to `api`.

choices.text: It resolves only after the TTL of the public record runs out
choices.why: Waiting changes nothing; the private zone answers first.

choices.text: It stops resolving there
choices.why: Right. The private zone answers "no such name".

prompt: Which half of the Private Resolver lets laptops in the office resolve `db.shop.internal`?
hint: Which direction does the question travel?

choices.text: The outbound endpoint, with a ruleset
choices.why: That sends Azure's questions to the office.

choices.text: The inbound endpoint
choices.why: Right. With a conditional forwarder for `shop.internal`.

choices.text: A link from the private zone to the office network
choices.why: Links join zones to virtual networks only.

choices.text: Neither: the office uses `168.63.129.16` directly
choices.why: That address answers only inside Azure.

prompt: A rule such as "questions for `corp.shop.example` go to `192.168.1.10`" belongs to a forwarding ___ on the outbound endpoint.
hint: A set of rules has a one-word name.

prompt: Put the steps of moving `shop.example` to Azure DNS in the safe order.
hint: The registrar changes last.
items: create the zone in Azure DNS
copy every record into the new zone
ask the new name servers directly with `dig @<server>`
write the four name servers at the registrar
wait for the parent's old NS records to expire
trap: Changing the registrar first sends the internet to a zone that is still empty.

prompt: A machine in `vnet-shop-staging` cannot resolve `db.shop.internal`, though one in `vnet-shop-prod` can. What is the first thing to check?
hint: Whom does the zone answer?

choices.text: The record's TTL
choices.why: TTL decides caching, not who may ask.

choices.text: Whether the zone has a link to `vnet-shop-staging`
choices.why: Right. The file linked production only.

choices.text: The zone's four name servers
choices.why: Private zones are not asked through name servers.

choices.text: Whether staging has registration enabled
choices.why: Registration writes names; resolving needs only a link.

prompt: Which of these did the lab actually do in this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Look at what has a transcript.

choices.text: Read a whole CNAME chain from the public DNS
choices.why: Right. `dig portal.azure.com`.

choices.text: Compiled a public zone with an alias record
choices.why: Right. `public.bicep`.

choices.text: Listed the name servers of a delegated zone with `dig NS`
choices.why: The recording machine's resolver left NS questions unanswered.

choices.text: Resolved `db.shop.internal` through a private zone
choices.why: Private zones answer only inside Azure.

choices.text: Compiled a private zone with automatic registration
choices.why: Right. `private.bicep`.
